statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-14670 (PostgreSQL plperl tied object heap buffer overflow executes arbitrary code) is fixed upstream in PostgreSQL 16.15 on the 16 branch: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-14670/ lists 16.15 as the fixed release for major version 16, the 16.15 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/16.15/, list this CVE, and the fix is commit https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/63cb15f40c6e4b5d74805e2f54231be09ac1783b (changing src/pl/plperl/plperl.c and contrib/hstore_plperl/hstore_plperl.c, tagged Security: CVE-2026-14670 and back-patched through 14). Alpine's postgresql16 APKBUILD on the 3.23-stable branch lists CVE-2026-14670 under its 16.15-r0 secfixes: https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/859fa0795e895af033fab32094a83301f2b4d8ff/community/postgresql16/APKBUILD. The DHI postgresql16 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built from Alpine's postgresql16 APKBUILD, which builds the upstream PostgreSQL release tarball and applies no security backports, and the postgres server binary in each published build reports its upstream release on both x86_64 and aarch64: 16.15-r0 and 16.16-r0 report PostgreSQL 16.15 and 16.16 and carry the fix, while the earlier published builds 16.13-r0 and 16.14-r0 report 16.13 and 16.14 and are affected. 16.15-r0 is the first published build that carries the fix.

PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-14670 (PostgreSQL plperl tied object heap buffer overflow executes arbitrary code) in 17.11 on the PostgreSQL 17 branch: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-14670/ lists 17.11 as the fixed release for major version 17, and the 17.11 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/17.11/, list this CVE. The fix is commit https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/2d78c34f8257d00f5fc65b8092c43dc77e246939 on the REL_17_STABLE branch, which changes src/pl/plperl/plperl.c and contrib/hstore_plperl/hstore_plperl.c so that array_to_datum_internal(), the helper plperl_array_to_datum() uses to convert a Perl array, takes each array's length from the value its caller already read instead of calling av_len() a second time, which is hazardous for tied arrays, and plperl_to_hstore() no longer relies on the entry count hv_iterinit() returns, which is not meaningful for a tied hash; it is tagged Security: CVE-2026-14670, and it is in the REL_17_11 release tag and not in REL_17_10. PL/Perl, /usr/lib/postgresql17/plperl.so, ships in the postgresql17-plperl package in every published build on both architectures. The DHI postgresql17 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built from Alpine's postgresql17 APKBUILD, currently https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/ce22298320177ae25085d86fbf3b4fc1150c16a2/main/postgresql17/APKBUILD, which builds the upstream PostgreSQL release tarball; none of the patches it applies touch the source files this fix changes. We checked the postgres server binary, /usr/libexec/postgresql17/postgres, in every published postgresql17 package for Alpine 3.23 on both x86_64 and aarch64 (checksums verified against the package index): 17.11-r0 and 17.12-r0 report PostgreSQL 17.11 and 17.12 and carry the fix, while the earlier builds 17.7-r0, 17.8-r0, 17.9-r0 and 17.10-r0 report 17.7, 17.8, 17.9 and 17.10 and are affected. This fix adds no distinctive message string, so the per-build evidence is the version each server binary reports. 17.11-r0 is the first published build that carries the fix. Alpine's postgresql17 APKBUILD lists CVE-2026-14670 under its 17.11-r0 secfixes.

PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-14670, a heap buffer overflow in PL/Perl's return of a tied hash that lets the function owner execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, in 17.11. Within major version 17, releases before 17.11 are affected. https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-14670/, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/17.11/. Debian fixed it for trixie in postgresql-17 17.11-0+deb13u1 (DSA-6438-1): https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-14670. The fixed version is this owner's first rebuild of Debian's 17.11-0+deb13u1, which packages PostgreSQL 17.11 and is no longer in the repository. Every build published now carries the fix: the postgres server binary reports PostgreSQL 17.11 in the current rebuild of Debian's 17.11-0+deb13u1 and in the 17.11-1 build, and PostgreSQL 17.12 in the 17.12-0 build and in the rebuild of Debian's 17.12-0+deb13u1, on amd64 and arm64. The earlier rebuild of Debian's 17.10-0+deb13u1, no longer in the repository, packages PostgreSQL 17.10; it is affected and sorts below the fixed version.
